answer.rationale: This scenario involves the introduction of a new hazardous chemical (solvent) into a workplace where employees will decant it into portable containers and have not been trained on its hazards. This squarely triggers HazCom requirements: the employer must maintain a written hazard communication program including a chemical inventory list (e), ensure workplace container labeling (f) — noting the portable-container exception for immediate-use transfers by the employee performing the transfer (f)(8), maintain SDS access (g), and provide effective information and training at the time a new chemical hazard is introduced into the work area, covering the specified training content elements (h). There is no indication this is a covered PSM process (no highly hazardous chemical process threshold information given), no LOTO-triggering task described (decanting is not machine servicing/energy control), and no indication of a recordable injury/illness, so PSM, LOTO, and Recordkeeping requirements are not applicable based on the facts given.
